20	If your Account receives incoming ACH transactions (either credits or debits) or wire transfers initiated from outside of the United States, both you and we are subject to the Operating Rules and Guidelines of the National Automated Clearing House Association (“NACHA”) or the rules of any wire transfer system involved....

Taking the Plaintiffs’ allegations as true, the Complaint raises a plausible claim that some number of the loans originated outside of the United States. 16	
17	```
18	The Defendants contend that the Complaint should be dismissed in its entirety for failure to comply with the 2004 Agreement’s dispute resolution and mediation clause. L.P./Inc. Mot. to Dismiss at 12-13. The clause provides that “[a]ny dispute, controversy or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement, or the breach, termination, or invalidity thereof shall first be referred by the parties to their senior-level executives for attempted resolution through good-faith negotiations.” Compl. Ex. A § 9.1 (emphasis added). Should negotiations fail, thirty days after making a written request to initiate those negotiations, “either Party may, by written notice to the other, require that the Dispute be referred to non-binding mediation administered by the American Arbitration Association.” Id. (emphasis added). The Defendants assert that Skold did not refer a dispute to a senior-level executive for negotiations and failed to make a written request that the dispute be referred to nonbinding mediation. L.P./Inc. Mot. to Dismiss at 12-13. Skold responds that the language of the mediation clause is permissive (“either Party may ... require”) and also argues that, in any event, Inc. has waived its right to invoke the clause because it participated in litigation over the dispute in the cancellation action before the TTAB. See Pl.’s L.P./Inc. Opp’n at 14-15.
19	The dispute resolution clause in the 2004 Agreement contains two clauses, one of which is mandatory (the parties shall refer the matter to senior executives to attempt to negotiate a resolution) and the other which is permissive (the parties may refer the matter to nonbinding mediation). Given the voluntary nature of the latter, this Court agrees with Skold that he was not required to refer this dispute to mediation before bringing suit here against Inc.
20	L.P. and S.A., who are not parties to the 2004 Agreement, also contend that the dispute resolution clause requires their dismissal from this action. In essence, they urge this Court to accept the contention that a nonparty to an agreement should be permitted to force a signatory party to engage in negotiations pursuant to a permissive mediation clause in that agreement as a condition precedent to filing suit but cite no relevant case or statute in support of this contention. See United States v. Benish, 5 F.3d 20, 26 (3d Cir.1993) (rejecting a party’s claim where the party “provided] no legal support for his argument or any persuasive reason” for the court to find in his favor). The Court sees no persuasive reason to dismiss Skold’s entire Complaint based on this unsupported argument. Accordingly, the motion to dismiss the Complaint against L.P. and S.A. on this ground shall be denied.
21	Regarding Inc.: although Skold did fail to bring in a senior-level executive to try to resolve the dispute — as he was required to do under the dispute resolution provision — Inc.’s participation in the TTAB proceedings waived any rights it may have had to seek to have the parties’ executives negotiate an end to the dispute. See, e.g., LBL Skysystems (USA), Inc. v. APG-Am., Inc., No. 02-5379, 2005 WL 2140240, at *30 (E.D.Pa. Aug. 31, 2005) (holding that a “party that engages in discovery and files pretrial motions waives a contract’s alternative dispute resolution provision”); Smith v. IMG Worldwide, Inc., 360 F.Supp.2d 681, 687 (E.D.Pa.2005) (finding that a party’s engaging in motion practice and providing “substantial discovery” constituted waiver of contractual alternative dispute resolution provision).
22	Viewing the four years’ worth of docket entries in the TTAB action, the Court considers that Inc. did not file a motion to stay the TTAB proceedings pending executive-level negotiations and instead filed, inter alia, motions to dismiss, a protective order, multiple summary judgment motions (one of which was partially granted in its favor), and a final brief in preparation for trial. See, e.g., Sköld v. Galderma Labs., Inc., Cancellation No. 92052897, 2012 WL 5902083 (T.T.A.B. Nov. 8, 2012) (granting Inc.’s motion for partial summary judgment on Skold’s abandonment claim). See also generally Registrant’s Trial Brief, Sköld v. Galderma Labs., Inc., Cancellation No. 92052897 (T.T.A.B. Aug. 13, 2014), Docket No. 81. This four-year history of litigation in the cancellation action — from filing nearly through trial — is, on its face, inconsistent with the notion that Inc. was willing to engage in the good-faith executive-level negotiations required by the dispute resolution provision.
23	Moreover, the Court can look to the TTAB’s grant of partial summary judgment in favor of Inc. and dismissing Skold’s abandonment claim as a concrete example of an instance where Inc.’s conduct inconsistent with the dispute resolution clause caused prejudice to Skold, not to mention the expenditure of time, cost, and resources attendant to maintaining a multi-year trademark cancellation action. The Defendants have undisputedly accepted the judicial process and have demonstrated that fact by: (1) Inc.’s failure to raise the issue of good-faith negotiations promptly before the TTAB; (2) Inc.’s engaging in discovery in the TTAB action; (3) Inc.’s filing of several pretrial motions in the TTAB action, none of which raise the issue of negotiation; and (4) the Defendants’ decision to wait until the case was ready to proceed to trial before the TTAB and until a Complaint was filed in this Court before asserting Skold’s failure to negotiate as grounds for a motion to dismiss. See St. Clair Area Sch. Dist. Bd. of Educ. v. E.I. Assocs., 733 A.2d 677, 682 n. 6 (Pa.Commw.Ct.1999) (“The key to determining whether [an alternative dispute resolution procedure] has been waived is whether the party, by virtue of its conduct, has accepted the judicial process.”). Inc. cannot now attempt to stand on the alternative dispute resolution clause as a reason for dismissal. Its right to invoke the clause has been waived.
24	```

Such examination shall be conducted, and CoJlaGenex shall make its records available, during normal business hours, after at least fifteen (15) days prior written notice to CollaGenex, as applicable, and shall take place at the facility(ies) where such records are maintained. Each such examination shall be limited to pertinent books and records for any year ending not more than twenty-four (24) months prior to the date of request; provided that Skold shall not be permitted to audit the same period of time more than once. Before permitting such independent accounting lirm to have access to such books and records, CollaGenex may require such independent accounting firm and its personnel involved in such audit, to signa confidentiality agreement (in form and substance reasonably acceptable to CollaGenex) as to any confidential information which is to be provided to such accounting firm or to which such accounting firm will have access, while conducting the audit under this paragraph. The clause provides that “[a]ny dispute, controversy or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement, or the breach, termination, or invalidity thereof shall first be referred by the parties to their senior-level executives for attempted resolution through good-faith negotiations.” Compl. Ex. A § 9.1 (emphasis added). Should negotiations fail, thirty days after making a written request to initiate those negotiations, “either Party may, by written notice to the other, require that the Dispute be referred to non-binding mediation administered by the American Arbitration Association.” Id. (emphasis added). The Defendants assert that Skold did not refer a dispute to a senior-level executive for negotiations and failed to make a written request that the dispute be referred to nonbinding mediation. L.P./Inc. Mot. to Dismiss at 12-13. Skold responds that the language of the mediation clause is permissive (“either Party may ... require”) and also argues that, in any event, Inc. has waived its right to invoke the clause because it participated in litigation over the dispute in the cancellation action before the TTAB. See Pl.’s L.P./Inc. Opp’n at 14-15.
The dispute resolution clause in the 2004 Agreement contains two clauses, one of which is mandatory (the parties shall refer the matter to senior executives to attempt to negotiate a resolution) and the other which is permissive (the parties may refer the matter to nonbinding mediation). Given the voluntary nature of the latter, this Court agrees with Skold that he was not required to refer this dispute to mediation before bringing suit here against Inc.
L.P. and S.A., who are not parties to the 2004 Agreement, also contend that the dispute resolution clause requires their dismissal from this action. In essence, they urge this Court to accept the contention that a nonparty to an agreement should be permitted to force a signatory party to engage in negotiations pursuant to a permissive mediation clause in that agreement as a condition precedent to filing suit but cite no relevant case or statute in support of this contention. See United States v. Benish, 5 F.3d 20, 26 (3d Cir.1993) (rejecting a party’s claim where the party “provided] no legal support for his argument or any persuasive reason” for the court to find in his favor). The Court sees no persuasive reason to dismiss Skold’s entire Complaint based on this unsupported argument. Accordingly, the motion to dismiss the Complaint against L.P. and S.A. on this ground shall be denied.
Regarding Inc.: although Skold did fail to bring in a senior-level executive to try to resolve the dispute — as he was required to do under the dispute resolution provision — Inc.’s participation in the TTAB proceedings waived any rights it may have had to seek to have the parties’ executives negotiate an end to the dispute. See, e.g., LBL Skysystems (USA), Inc. v. APG-Am., Inc., No. 02-5379, 2005 WL 2140240, at *30 (E.D.Pa. Aug. 31, 2005) (holding that a “party that engages in discovery and files pretrial motions waives a contract’s alternative dispute resolution provision”); Smith v. IMG Worldwide, Inc., 360 F.Supp.2d 681, 687 (E.D.Pa.2005) (finding that a party’s engaging in motion practice and providing “substantial discovery” constituted waiver of contractual alternative dispute resolution provision).
Viewing the four years’ worth of docket entries in the TTAB action, the Court considers that Inc. did not file a motion to stay the TTAB proceedings pending executive-level negotiations and instead filed, inter alia, motions to dismiss, a protective order, multiple summary judgment motions (one of which was partially granted in its favor), and a final brief in preparation for trial. See, e.g., Sköld v. Galderma Labs., Inc., Cancellation No. 92052897, 2012 WL 5902083 (T.T.A.B. Nov. 8, 2012) (granting Inc.’s motion for partial summary judgment on Skold’s abandonment claim). See also generally Registrant’s Trial Brief, Sköld v. Galderma Labs., Inc., Cancellation No. 92052897 (T.T.A.B. Aug. 13, 2014), Docket No. 81. This four-year history of litigation in the cancellation action — from filing nearly through trial — is, on its face, inconsistent with the notion that Inc. was willing to engage in the good-faith executive-level negotiations required by the dispute resolution provision.
Moreover, the Court can look to the TTAB’s grant of partial summary judgment in favor of Inc. and dismissing Skold’s abandonment claim as a concrete example of an instance where Inc.’s conduct inconsistent with the dispute resolution clause caused prejudice to Skold, not to mention the expenditure of time, cost, and resources attendant to maintaining a multi-year trademark cancellation action. The Defendants have undisputedly accepted the judicial process and have demonstrated that fact by: (1) Inc.’s failure to raise the issue of good-faith negotiations promptly before the TTAB; (2) Inc.’s engaging in discovery in the TTAB action; (3) Inc.’s filing of several pretrial motions in the TTAB action, none of which raise the issue of negotiation; and (4) the Defendants’ decision to wait until the case was ready to proceed to trial before the TTAB and until a Complaint was filed in this Court before asserting Skold’s failure to negotiate as grounds for a motion to dismiss. See St. Clair Area Sch. Dist. Bd. of Educ. v. E.I. Assocs., 733 A.2d 677, 682 n. 6 (Pa.Commw.Ct.1999) (“The key to determining whether [an alternative dispute resolution procedure] has been waived is whether the party, by virtue of its conduct, has accepted the judicial process.”). Inc. cannot now attempt to stand on the alternative dispute resolution clause as a reason for dismissal. Its right to invoke the clause has been waived.

{"judgments": [
{"clause_id":"c001","reasoning_cat1":"The parenthetical defining \"Manager\" is broken (“Managers Fund and Manager each being referred to…”), so the defined term is introduced by a mangled clause, and the joint-and-several designation of two entities as one \"Borrower\" is a recurring source of argument.","reasoning_cat2":"Checked against Section 16.11 (Manager as Administrative Borrower) and Section 2.13 (joint and several liability), which are consistent with the preamble's designations.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.10},
{"clause_id":"c002","reasoning_cat1":"A pure incorporation of the UCC definition with nothing to construe.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the \"Code\" definition and Section 4.1's grant of security interest.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.03},
{"clause_id":"c003","reasoning_cat1":"Broad but definite; it enumerates the capacities (obligor on an Account, chattel paper, General Intangible, or maker of a Note Receivable) without a residual catch-all.","reasoning_cat2":"Checked against the Eligible Notes Receivable concentration limit (clause (u)) which uses \"same Account Debtor\"; the definitions fit.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c004","reasoning_cat1":"Definite and bounded by the parenthetical example; \"or related services\" is mildly open but functionally harmless.","reasoning_cat2":"Fits the \"Bank Product\" and \"Bank Product Provider\" definitions without tension.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c005","reasoning_cat1":"A one-line pointer definition with nothing ambiguous on its face.","reasoning_cat2":"The cross-reference to Section 4.4(c) is accurate; that subsection does define \"Additional Documents\".","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.03},
{"clause_id":"c006","reasoning_cat1":"Pure pointer definition.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 2.1(a) does define \"Advance\" and \"Advances\"; no mismatch found.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.03},
{"clause_id":"c007","reasoning_cat1":"Pure pointer definition.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 16.11 does appoint Manager as Administrative Borrower, matching this reference.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.03},
{"clause_id":"c008","reasoning_cat1":"\"Control\" is defined by the vague standard \"power to direct the management and policies… by contract, or otherwise,\" and the proviso then deems 10% holders, directors and joint venturers to be Affiliates only for two purposes, creating a general-versus-specific tension about the term's reach elsewhere.","reasoning_cat2":"The dual definition drives Eligible Notes Receivable clause (k) and Section 7.13 (Transactions with Affiliates) with a different meaning than it carries in Section 6.12 and \"Bank Product Provider,\" a real risk of inconsistent application.","prob_cat1":0.28,"prob_cat2":0.14},
{"clause_id":"c009","reasoning_cat1":"Pure pointer definition.","reasoning_cat2":"The preamble does define \"Agreement\"; no conflict.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.03},
{"clause_id":"c010","reasoning_cat1":"Two fixed percentages tied to two loan types; the words and numerals agree.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 2.5(a) and Section 2.10(e), which both invoke the Applicable Margin.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c011","reasoning_cat1":"Clause (b) sets a zero percent premium after the first anniversary, which makes the defined \"premium\" a nullity for most of the term — odd but arithmetically clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 3.7(a) says termination requires payment \"together with the Applicable Prepayment Premium\" while 3.7(b) says \"if applicable,\" leaving a small inconsistency about whether a zero premium is still a condition.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.14},
{"clause_id":"c012","reasoning_cat1":"The trailing catch-all \"together with any obligations undertaken or assumed relating thereto\" is open-ended against the two enumerated sources, and \"Permitted reorganization\" is inconsistently capitalised.","reasoning_cat2":"Checked against \"Permitted Reorganization,\" \"Subordinated Debt\" (which requires unsecured debt) and Permitted Liens clause (c); Approved Debt is permitted to be secured, so the definitions only just cohere.","prob_cat1":0.25,"prob_cat2":0.17},
{"clause_id":"c013","reasoning_cat1":"The clause layers \"approval will not be unreasonably withheld\" against a Lender right to remove companies \"in its reasonable discretion,\" leaving the standard for removal contestable.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 5.21 and Schedule 5.21 supply the list; consistent, though the office/agent geographic limit interacts with the Settlement Agent definition without conflict.","prob_cat1":0.17,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c014","reasoning_cat1":"Pure pointer definition.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 14.1(a) does define \"Assignee\"; no mismatch.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.03},
{"clause_id":"c015","reasoning_cat1":"The three alternatives are disjunctive, so clause (b) (\"otherwise acceptable to Lender\") and clause (c) (\"an informal or unwritten estimate of value by Servicer\") swallow the FIRREA standard in clause (a) — a classic general-versus-specific defect.","reasoning_cat2":"It feeds Section 3.1(t)(viii), Section 2.1(b) valuation reserves and Eligible Notes Receivable clause (r)(vii), where a mere unwritten Servicer estimate sits awkwardly with the demand for \"current Authorized Appraisal\" documentation.","prob_cat1":0.34,"prob_cat2":0.18},
{"clause_id":"c016","reasoning_cat1":"A closed list of five named individuals plus the sitting CFO of Manager; definite, though OCR-garbled names could be argued.","reasoning_cat2":"Overlaps but is not identical to \"Executive Officer\" and \"Validity Agreement Party\"; the near-duplication invites argument about which list governs Section 2.2 borrowing requests.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c017","reasoning_cat1":"Defined by reference to what Borrowers \"are entitled to borrow\" after reserves and sublimits, which is circular but conventional.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 2.1(a) and 2.1(c) and the Borrowing Base definition.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c018","reasoning_cat1":"\"Any financial accommodation… including: (a)–(g)\" pairs a very broad genus with a specific list, so the reach of the general words beyond the enumerated services is genuinely uncertain.","reasoning_cat2":"Bank Product Obligations are excluded from \"Availability\" and from Section 2.5 interest but included in \"Obligations\"; the boundary matters and is not resolved elsewhere.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c019","reasoning_cat1":"Straightforward and definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the \"Loan Documents\" definition, which includes Bank Product Agreements, and with Section 15.1's carve-out for them.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c020","reasoning_cat1":"Long but carefully catalogued; the sweeping \"irrespective of whether\" language is standard.","reasoning_cat2":"Fits Section 2.3(b)(D)/(F) application waterfall and Section 3.6's cash-collateral requirement.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c021","reasoning_cat1":"A two-word definite designation.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 16.8(b) and Section 4.1's grant for the benefit of Bank Product Providers.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c022","reasoning_cat1":"The amount is whatever \"Lender has established\" based on the providers' \"reasonable determination,\" a soft standard but a familiar one.","reasoning_cat2":"The Borrowing Base deducts this reserve, yet Section 2.1(b) promises Lender will not establish reserves until a Triggering Event; whether that promise reaches the Bank Product Reserve is unresolved.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.20},
{"clause_id":"c023","reasoning_cat1":"Pure statutory reference.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the \"Insolvency Proceeding\" definition and Section 8.4/8.5.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.03},
{"clause_id":"c024","reasoning_cat1":"Mechanically detailed; the \"conclusive in the absence of manifest error\" tag is a familiar and rarely contested formula.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the \"LIBOR Rate\" and \"Interest Period\" definitions and Section 2.12.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c025","reasoning_cat1":"\"Prime rate\" is expressly explained as not necessarily the lowest rate, which forecloses the usual argument.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with \"Base Rate Loan\" and Section 2.5(d)'s automatic adjustment mechanic.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c026","reasoning_cat1":"Simple and definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 2.5(a) and 2.12(a).","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.03},
{"clause_id":"c027","reasoning_cat1":"Pure form reference.","reasoning_cat2":"Exhibit B-1 exists and is in the stated form; no mismatch.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c028","reasoning_cat1":"Tied to ERISA statutory definitions with a fixed six-year lookback; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 5.13's representation that no Benefit Plan is maintained.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c029","reasoning_cat1":"Definite and self-explanatory for an LLC context.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 3.1(c) and Section 6.3(d)(vi).","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.03},
{"clause_id":"c030","reasoning_cat1":"Broad but exhaustively descriptive; nothing turns on a contested word.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Borrower Collateral clause (b) and the inspection right in Section 4.6.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c031","reasoning_cat1":"\"A reference to each of and either of Fund and Manager\" is grammatically odd and could be read either distributively or collectively, which matters for every covenant phrased in the singular.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 1.2 says \"Borrower\" in financial covenants means Fund and its Subsidiaries consolidated, and Section 7.16 measures Fund's Tangible Net Worth only — an overlay that this definition does not itself acknowledge.","prob_cat1":0.22,"prob_cat2":0.18},
{"clause_id":"c032","reasoning_cat1":"It opens with \"all property, including, without limitation, each of the following\" and then lists twelve categories that conspicuously omit Real Property, leaving genuinely open whether foreclosed Real Estate Owned is Borrower Collateral — a textbook general-versus-specific problem.","reasoning_cat2":"\"Collateral\" separately sweeps in \"all other assets… in or upon which a Lien is granted,\" and Permitted Dispositions clause (g) allows sale of Real Estate Owned, so the instrument as a whole is unclear whether Lender's lien reaches acquired real property.","prob_cat1":0.36,"prob_cat2":0.28},
{"clause_id":"c033","reasoning_cat1":"Defines the procedures by reference to an undelivered external document and makes amendments subject to Lender's \"sole discretion\"; the content is not fixed in the instrument.","reasoning_cat2":"These procedures are the operative yardstick for Eligible Notes Receivable clauses (b),(d),(e) and Sections 4.8, 6.5 and 7.9, so any gap in them propagates widely.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c034","reasoning_cat1":"Trivially definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 2.1 and 2.2.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.03},
{"clause_id":"c035","reasoning_cat1":"A clean two-line formula: 20% of Net Eligible Notes Receivable minus specified reserves.","reasoning_cat2":"The reserve deduction cross-refers to Section 2.1(b), which itself promises no reserves absent a Triggering Event while Section 10 lets Lender set reserves against the Borrowing Base on any failure to pay third persons — a genuine tension about what may be deducted.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c036","reasoning_cat1":"Definite in structure, but it defines the certificate by reference to a form that is not supplied.","reasoning_cat2":"Exhibit B-2 in the executed document reads only \"[form to be provided by Lender]\", so the required content of a condition-precedent deliverable (Section 3.3(f)) is left to be fixed later.","prob_cat1":0.15,"prob_cat2":0.22},
{"clause_id":"c037","reasoning_cat1":"Two named states and the usual weekend carve-out; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Dallas-time deadlines in Sections 2.2, 2.3 and 2.7, although the closing-day reference is to New York and California rather than Texas.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c038","reasoning_cat1":"Defined by GAAP; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with \"Indebtedness\" clause (c) and \"Purchase Money Indebtedness\".","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.03},
{"clause_id":"c039","reasoning_cat1":"Defined by GAAP; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with \"Capitalized Lease Obligation\" and Permitted Liens clause (e).","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.03},
{"clause_id":"c040","reasoning_cat1":"A long enumerated list with objective ratings and dollar thresholds; the sub-lettering in clause (e) is garbled but the substance is clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Permitted Investments clause (a) and Permitted Dispositions clause (c).","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c041","reasoning_cat1":"Pure pointer definition.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 2.6(a) does define \"Cash Management Account\"; accurate.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c042","reasoning_cat1":"\"Form and substance satisfactory to Lender\" is a soft standard but the parties to the agreements are specified.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 2.6(e) requires Escrow Accounts to be subject to a Cash Management Agreement \"with Lender and Borrowers,\" while this definition contemplates a tripartite agreement including a Cash Management Bank — a small mismatch.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.14},
{"clause_id":"c043","reasoning_cat1":"Pure pointer definition.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 2.6(a) does define \"Cash Management Bank\"; accurate.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c044","reasoning_cat1":"Four objective triggers stated in absolute 100% terms; definite but unforgiving.","reasoning_cat2":"\"Permitted Holders\" names only four individuals while \"Validity Agreement Party\" names five, and \"Permitted Reorganization\" expressly contemplates admitting Manager, Servicer and their affiliates as members — so an approved reorganisation could itself trip clause (a) or (d).","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.26},
{"clause_id":"c045","reasoning_cat1":"One sentence, entirely definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 3.4's three-year term measured from the Closing Date.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.03},
{"clause_id":"c046","reasoning_cat1":"Definite; defined by issuer and subject.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the \"Settlement Agent\" definition, which relies on it.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c047","reasoning_cat1":"The proviso carefully allocates which jurisdiction's UCC governs which issue; well drafted.","reasoning_cat2":"Sits alongside Section 13's New York governing law while the Borrowers and much of the Note Receivable Collateral are Californian, but the proviso is designed to handle exactly that.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.11},

{"clause_id":"c050","reasoning_cat1":"\"All cash, checks, notes, instruments, and other items of payment\" pairs enumerated specifics with an open catch-all, and the parenthetical of examples (insurance proceeds, rental proceeds, tax refunds) does not bound it.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 2.6(a)(ii) requires all Collections to be deposited within one Business Day and Section 4.3 requires them held in trust, so the scope of \"Collections\" carries real consequences.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.12},
{"clause_id":"c049","reasoning_cat1":"Enumerates three document types from \"any lessor, warehouseman, processor, consignee, or other Person in possession\" — a mild ejusdem generis question with an express Account Debtor carve-out.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 6.9 requires a Collateral Access Agreement on relocation and Section 7.15 bars bailee storage with a public-warehouse proviso; broadly consistent.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c051","reasoning_cat1":"Pure pointer definition.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 4.4(b) does define the term; accurate.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.03},
{"clause_id":"c052","reasoning_cat1":"Definite; a form certificate signed by a specified officer.","reasoning_cat2":"The definition requires signature by the CFO of Administrative Borrower, while Exhibit C-1 is executed by \"the undersigned officer of Manager\" generally — a small mismatch.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.10},
{"clause_id":"c053","reasoning_cat1":"Definite as to parties and subject; \"satisfactory to Lender\" is the only soft element.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 4.7 and Section 2.6(d) both require Control Agreements, and Schedule D-1 requires the Designated Account be subject to one; consistent.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.05},

{"judgments": [
{"clause_id":"c061","reasoning_cat1":"Definite as to author and subject; only \"satisfactory to Lender\" is soft.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 3.1(b)(v) requires a Disbursement Letter for the initial Advance and Section 2.2(b) governs funding; consistent.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c062","reasoning_cat1":"Trivially definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 2.4 and Eligible Notes Receivable clause (m).","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.03},
{"clause_id":"c063","reasoning_cat1":"The gateway to the entire Borrowing Base: it sets nineteen exclusions but lets Lender modify the criteria \"in Lender's Permitted Discretion\" and re-include anything \"following a review thereof on a case-by-case basis,\" and the opening parenthesis of that carve-out is never closed; clause (a) also requires the loan to have been \"originated by Servicer but is now held by Fund.\"","reasoning_cat2":"It is repeated as a representation in Section 5.2, fixes the $250,000,000 delivery conditions in Sections 3.1(t), 3.3(e), 4.2 and 8.17, and its origination requirement sits against the broader \"Note Receivable\" definition that covers loans Fund merely purchased.","prob_cat1":0.45,"prob_cat2":0.32},
{"clause_id":"c064","reasoning_cat1":"An enumerated list with numeric thresholds; clause (c) drops the dollar sign before 250,000,000, a small mechanical slip.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 14.1(a) permits assignment to a non-Eligible Transferee in a portfolio sale, which is expressly carved out; consistent.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c065","reasoning_cat1":"A long specific list ending in \"or other communication,\" which is a broad residual against enumerated formal instruments.","reasoning_cat2":"Feeds Section 6.13(d)(ii) notice duties and the Section 11.3 indemnity without conflict.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c066","reasoning_cat1":"Catalogues statutes but opens with an unbounded genus including \"binding and enforceable guideline\" and \"binding and enforceable written policy\".","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 5.14 and 6.13 and the \"Remedial Action\" definition.","prob_cat1":0.15,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c067","reasoning_cat1":"Sweeps in punitive, consequential and treble damages plus \"fines, penalties, sanctions\"; broad but itemised.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the \"Environmental Lien\" definition and Section 11.3(c).","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c068","reasoning_cat1":"Short and definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 6.13(a) requires the property be kept free of Environmental Liens; consistent.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c069","reasoning_cat1":"UCC definition expanded by an illustrative list with an express exclusion of consumer goods, farm products and Inventory; well bounded.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Borrower Collateral clause (e), Section 5.4 and Permitted Dispositions clause (a).","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c070","reasoning_cat1":"Pure statutory reference.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Benefit Plan and ERISA Affiliate definitions and Section 5.13.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.03},
{"clause_id":"c071","reasoning_cat1":"Tied to specific IRC sections; technical but definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 5.13.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c072","reasoning_cat1":"Pure pointer definition.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 2.6(e) creates the Escrow Account but excepts \"accounts belonging to an Account Debtor,\" whereas Section 6.17 requires deposit of all funds held on behalf of any Account Debtor — the two do not sit together.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.22},

{"clause_id":"c075","reasoning_cat1":"A closed list of five named individuals; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"It overlaps but does not coincide with \"Permitted Holders\" (four names) and \"Authorized Person\" (five names plus the CFO), and Section 8.13 makes departure of any Executive Officer a default — the near-identical but unequal lists invite argument.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.15},
{"clause_id":"c076","reasoning_cat1":"Definite as to author and purpose.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 3.1(a) requires delivery of the letter and Section 4.4(a) separately authorises filings; consistent.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c077","reasoning_cat1":"Pure pointer definition.","reasoning_cat2":"The preamble does define \"Fund\"; accurate.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.03},

{"judgments": [
{"clause_id":"c146","reasoning_cat1":"The numerator is \"all Obligations of Borrower\" while the denominator, Tangible Net Worth, is defined by reference to Fund alone, so the ratio mixes two different measuring entities.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 7.16(b) caps this ratio at 0.9%, which against the $600,000,000 Tangible Net Worth floor permits roughly $5.4 million of Obligations — impossible to reconcile with the $50,000,000 Maximum Revolver Amount and Section 2.1(a).","prob_cat1":0.21,"prob_cat2":0.36},
{"clause_id":"c147","reasoning_cat1":"A named corporation; nothing to construe.","reasoning_cat2":"The \"Subsidiary\" proviso expressly excludes Bar-K, yet \"Change of Control\" clause (c) requires Permitted Holders to own 100% of Servicer's Stock — Servicer is treated as both inside and outside the credit group.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.14},
{"clause_id":"c148","reasoning_cat1":"Names the parties and subject matter; the singular \"Borrower\" where two Borrowers exist is a small looseness.","reasoning_cat2":"It is a Loan Document and a Section 3.1(b)(iv) closing condition, and Sections 4.8, 8.15 and 9.1(e)/(o) all depend on it; consistent in substance.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.10},
{"clause_id":"c149","reasoning_cat1":"The alternative branch — \"any settlement agent (including a title company, title agency, attorney or law firm) covered by a Closing Protection Letter\" — is a general category qualified by a list, and the escrow-instruction condition is embedded rather than separately stated.","reasoning_cat2":"Sections 2.2(b), 3.1(t)(iv) and 6.18 rely on the term; the Approved Title Insurance Company definition supplies the letter, so the structure holds together.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c150","reasoning_cat1":"A bare balance-sheet test (\"assets greater than… debts\") stated \"at fair valuations,\" omitting the usual unreasonably-small-capital and ability-to-pay prongs; the truncation is itself a construction question.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 5.12(a) represents Solvency and Section 5.12(b) separately addresses fraudulent transfer intent, and Eligible Notes Receivable clause (q) applies the test to makers; no direct conflict found.","prob_cat1":0.21,"prob_cat2":0.10},
{"clause_id":"c151","reasoning_cat1":"It sweeps options, warrants and \"other equivalents (regardless of how designated)\" into \"Stock,\" so a test phrased as owning \"100% of the Stock\" becomes hard to satisfy or apply.","reasoning_cat2":"\"Change of Control\" clauses (b)-(d) demand ownership of 100% of the Stock of Manager, Servicer and each Subsidiary, and Restricted Payments clause (c) separately addresses warrants and options — the breadth of this definition strains those tests.","prob_cat1":0.23,"prob_cat2":0.18},
{"clause_id":"c152","reasoning_cat1":"Clause (a) is confined to \"unsecured Indebtedness,\" which is a clear limit but an odd one given clause (b).","reasoning_cat2":"The \"Subordinated Note\" definition describes notes evidencing Approved Debt as \"secured by the assets of Fund,\" and Permitted Liens clause (c) allows liens for Approved Debt, so secured paper counts as Subordinated Debt through clause (b) despite clause (a)'s unsecured requirement; Tangible Net Worth then adds Subordinated Debt back to equity.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.23},
{"clause_id":"c153","reasoning_cat1":"The cap is defined by a long parenthetical accounting formula that expressly leaves the treatment of unrealised gains and losses \"in Manager's discretion,\" so the permitted principal amount is not objectively ascertainable.","reasoning_cat2":"It describes the note as \"secured by the assets of Fund,\" which sits against the \"Subordinated Debt\" requirement of unsecured Indebtedness and against Section 7.2's negative pledge except for Permitted Liens.","prob_cat1":0.30,"prob_cat2":0.27},
{"clause_id":"c154","reasoning_cat1":"Two clearly differentiated forms with specified signatories; \"satisfactory to Lender\" is the only soft term.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Permitted Reorganization clause (b), Section 7.7(b) and Section 7.10(b).","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c155","reasoning_cat1":"The proviso excludes from \"Subsidiary\" any entity formed after the Closing Date that is not funded with Borrower assets, any New Fund, and Bar-K — a set of carve-outs broad enough to swallow the general rule, and \"capitalized or otherwise funded with assets of such Borrower\" is itself vague.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 7.13 forbids forming or acquiring \"any Subsidiary\" without Lender's consent, but the proviso means most newly formed entities are simply not Subsidiaries, so the covenant and the whole raft of \"and its Subsidiaries\" obligations can be sidestepped.","prob_cat1":0.33,"prob_cat2":0.36},
{"clause_id":"c156","reasoning_cat1":"Tracks the UCC concept with an enumerated list of supported obligations.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Borrower Collateral clause (j).","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c157","reasoning_cat1":"A formula, but the connector between the two halves is garbled in this text and the definition adds Subordinated Debt back into equity — an unusual construction that could be read either way if the operator were in doubt.","reasoning_cat2":"It is the denominator of the Senior Leverage Ratio and the subject of Section 7.16(a)'s $600,000,000 floor and Section 3.1(n)'s closing condition; the interaction with the 0.9% ratio cap produces an impossible result.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.20},
{"clause_id":"c158","reasoning_cat1":"The closing words \"attributable to the taxable income or gain of such Borrower\" have no clear antecedent, since the distributing entity was described as \"Fund or Manager\" and the recipients as \"holders of its Stock\".","reasoning_cat2":"Section 7.10(a)(i) permits Tax Distributions subject to delivery of quarterly financials; consistent in structure.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.12},
{"clause_id":"c159","reasoning_cat1":"Pure pointer definition.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 16.5 does define \"Taxes\"; accurate.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.03},
{"clause_id":"c160","reasoning_cat1":"Clause (a) says a Triggering Event exists if \"an Event of Default has occurred,\" with no requirement that it be continuing or uncured — a once-and-forever trigger on the face of the words.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 2.1(b) then conditions reserves on a Triggering Event having \"occurred and is continuing,\" which the definition does not accommodate; the $500,000,000 portfolio test in clause (b) also sits oddly with the $600,000,000 net worth covenant.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.22},
{"clause_id":"c161","reasoning_cat1":"Trivially definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Used consistently throughout.","prob_cat1":0.02,"prob_cat2":0.02},

{"clause_id":"c163","reasoning_cat1":"A closed list of five named individuals.","reasoning_cat2":"It names a fifth individual (Stephanie Ng Kelly) who is not a \"Permitted Holder,\" which matters because the Change of Control test requires Permitted Holders to own 100% of Manager and Servicer.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.15},

{"clause_id":"c166","reasoning_cat1":"The final sentence redefines \"Borrower\" for financial covenants to mean Fund and its Subsidiaries consolidated \"unless the context clearly requires otherwise\" — an escape hatch with no ascertainable boundary.","reasoning_cat2":"It collides with the \"Borrower\" definition (\"each of and either of Fund and Manager\") and with the Senior Leverage Ratio, which measures Obligations of \"Borrower\" against Fund-only Tangible Net Worth.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.26},
{"clause_id":"c167","reasoning_cat1":"A clear tie-breaker rule preferring Article 9 definitions.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the \"Code\" definition's own multi-jurisdiction proviso and with Section 4.7's reference to Sections 8-106 and 9-104 et seq.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c168","reasoning_cat1":"It legislates that \"including\" is non-limiting and \"or\" means \"and/or,\" which displaces the ordinary interpretive canons and is itself a frequent battleground where lists are involved.","reasoning_cat2":"It sits with Section 16.2 (headings) and Section 16.3 (no construction against either party) and applies to the many enumerated lists in this document, notably \"Borrower Collateral\" and \"Loan Documents\".","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c169","reasoning_cat1":"One sentence incorporating attached schedules and exhibits; the qualifier \"attached\" is the only limit.","reasoning_cat2":"Exhibit B-2 (the Borrowing Base Certificate) is not in fact attached — it reads \"[form to be provided by Lender]\" — so an incorporated exhibit central to Section 3.3(f) has no content.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.22},
{"clause_id":"c170","reasoning_cat1":"A clean \"lesser of\" formula between two defined amounts.","reasoning_cat2":"The $50,000,000 ceiling cannot be squared with Section 7.16(b)'s 0.9% Senior Leverage Ratio cap measured against a $600,000,000 Tangible Net Worth floor.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.28},
{"clause_id":"c171","reasoning_cat1":"The provision grants an unrestricted Permitted Discretion right to set reserves and then, two sentences later, promises not to set any reserve absent a Triggering Event — the grant and the promise pull in opposite directions within the same subsection.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 10(b) separately lets Lender \"set up such reserves against the Borrowing Base or the Maximum Revolver Amount as Lender deems necessary\" with no Triggering Event condition, and the parenthetical about liens \"specifically identified\" on Schedule P-1 as having priority describes a designation Schedule P-1 does not actually make.","prob_cat1":0.36,"prob_cat2":0.42},
{"clause_id":"c172","reasoning_cat1":"The second limit — that availability plus cash in the Cash Management Accounts may not exceed Fund's unfunded commitments to makers — is counter-intuitive and its arithmetic purpose is not stated, leaving room for opposed readings.","reasoning_cat2":"It interacts with the Borrowing Base, Section 2.4 Overadvances and Section 6.18's requirement to fund subsequent disbursements directly, but no other provision explains the unfunded-commitment cap.","prob_cat1":0.28,"prob_cat2":0.20},
{"clause_id":"c173","reasoning_cat1":"A one-sentence revolving-credit statement.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 2.1(a), 3.4 and 3.6.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c174","reasoning_cat1":"Plain and definite, with an express non-exclusive reference to Section 3.3.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 3.3 does set the conditions precedent to all extensions of credit; consistent.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c175","reasoning_cat1":"It requires a written request by noon on the very day of funding, permits telephonic notice \"at Lender's election,\" and then says failure to confirm in writing \"shall not affect the validity of the request\" — a set of mechanics whose interaction is not obvious.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 2.8 separately authorises Advances on instructions from \"anyone purporting to be an Authorized Person,\" which is a looser standard than this subsection's requirement of an actual Authorized Person.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c176","reasoning_cat1":"Definite as to timing and destination of funds.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 2.8, Schedule D-1 and the Settlement Agent definition.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.07},

{"clause_id":"c178","reasoning_cat1":"A long, carefully ordered waterfall with defined terms and an internal definition of \"paid in full\"; the kind of provision that is detailed rather than ambiguous.","reasoning_cat2":"Subsection (iv) expressly anticipates and resolves conflicts with other Loan Documents in favour of this Section, which reduces rather than creates whole-instrument risk.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.12},
{"clause_id":"c179","reasoning_cat1":"Defines \"Overadvance\" by reference to \"any of the limitations set forth in Section 2.1,\" which includes the opaque unfunded-commitment test in 2.1(c).","reasoning_cat2":"Section 2.3(b)(D) restrains Lender from an election that would create an Overadvance, and Section 2.1(c) supplies the limits; the chain is consistent but depends on 2.1(c)'s unclear second limb.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c180","reasoning_cat1":"A two-branch rate formula tied to defined terms.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 2.12 and the Applicable Margin definition.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c181","reasoning_cat1":"The default rate is set at four points over the rate applicable to Base Rate Loans even for LIBOR Rate Loans, and it applies only \"at the election of Lender\" without saying how that election is made or communicated.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 2.12(a) lets Lender convert LIBOR loans to Base Rate on default, which partly explains the reference, but the two elections are not linked.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c182","reasoning_cat1":"It authorises Lender to charge everything to the Loan Account and to compound unpaid interest into new Advances — commercially aggressive but stated in plain terms.","reasoning_cat2":"The opening carve-out \"Except as provided to the contrary in Section 2.10\" is loose because Section 2.10 sets several different payment dates; otherwise consistent with Sections 2.9 and 2.5(e).","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c183","reasoning_cat1":"A 360-day convention plus automatic rate adjustment; arithmetically definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Base Rate definition and Section 2.5(e)'s usury savings clause.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.06},

{"clause_id":"c185","reasoning_cat1":"Detailed and mandatory, but the numbering is garbled and the final sentence imposes a flat 60-day migration to Wells Fargo that the preceding clauses (referring to \"one or more\" banks on Schedule 2.6) do not anticipate.","reasoning_cat2":"Schedule 2.6 names Greater Bay Bank and The Mechanics Bank, and Section 2.6(c) lets Administrative Borrower add or replace Cash Management Banks — both hard to reconcile with the requirement that Wells Fargo be the only one after 60 days.","prob_cat1":0.17,"prob_cat2":0.26},
{"clause_id":"c186","reasoning_cat1":"Specifies three required terms of the agreements; definite though \"among other things\" leaves the balance open.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 2.6(e) requires a Cash Management Agreement \"with Lender and Borrowers\" for Escrow Accounts while this subsection contemplates the bank as a party; a small mismatch in described parties.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.13},

{"clause_id":"c188","reasoning_cat1":"A short, unambiguous lien grant.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 4.1, Borrower Collateral clause (d) and Section 4.7's control requirement.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c189","reasoning_cat1":"It defines \"Escrow Account\" as a deposit account and then repeatedly refers to \"such Cash Management Account,\" and the carve-out for \"accounts belonging to an Account Debtor of Borrower\" has no defined boundary.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 6.17 affirmatively requires deposit into a Lender-lien deposit account of \"all amounts delivered to any Borrower to be held on behalf of any Account Debtor,\" which is the very category this subsection excepts.","prob_cat1":0.30,"prob_cat2":0.34},
{"clause_id":"c190","reasoning_cat1":"A precise conditional-receipt rule with a stated cut-off; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 2.3(a) and 2.9 and with Schedule L-1's designation of Lender's Account.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c191","reasoning_cat1":"It authorises Advances on instructions \"from anyone purporting to be an Authorized Person,\" a striking risk allocation, and the sentence contains a duplicated verb (\"agrees to establish establish\").","reasoning_cat2":"Section 2.2(a) requires a request \"by an Authorized Person,\" so the two provisions state different standards for who may bind Borrowers.","prob_cat1":0.22,"prob_cat2":0.18},
{"clause_id":"c192","reasoning_cat1":"An account-stated clause with a 30-day objection window and a manifest-error carve-out; standard and definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 2.5(c) and 2.7 and the Lender Expenses definition.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c193","reasoning_cat1":"A fixed dollar fee, fully earned on a stated date.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the non-refundability preamble to Section 2.10 and Section 3.1(l).","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c194","reasoning_cat1":"The sentence is missing its noun — \"a monthly loan administration equal to $2,000\" — so the thing being charged is never named.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 2.5(c) authorises charging \"all fees and costs provided for in Section 2.10\" to the Loan Account, which supplies the mechanism if not the noun.","prob_cat1":0.21,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c195","reasoning_cat1":"The rate is written as \"one-half of one percent (0.30%)\" — the words and the numeral state two different figures — and the sub-clause labels (\"(A)… or (y)\") do not match, so the fee cannot be computed from the text alone.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 2.10(e) uses the same $20,000,000 floor for the Minimum Interest Period charge, so the two fees may double-count the same shortfall.","prob_cat1":0.56,"prob_cat2":0.17},
{"clause_id":"c196","reasoning_cat1":"Specific per-day fee plus actual third-party charges; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"The Lender Expenses definition caps audit and appraisal charges \"up to the amount of any limitation contained in this Agreement,\" and this is that limitation; consistent.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c197","reasoning_cat1":"A detailed hypothetical-interest calculation; complex but each input is defined, and the usury proviso is express.","reasoning_cat2":"It overlaps with the Section 2.10(c) unused line fee, which also uses the $20,000,000 Minimum Interest Period floor, so a Borrower could argue duplicate charging.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.16},

{"judgments": [
{"clause_id":"c206","reasoning_cat1":"The substance (other Borrowers must cover a defaulting Borrower's payment) is plain, though the subsection is lettered \"(a)\" where it should be \"(c)\".","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 2.13(a)-(b) and the preamble's joint and several designation.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c207","reasoning_cat1":"It cross-refers to \"Section 2.15,\" a section that does not exist, and declares the obligations enforceable \"irrespective of the validity… of this Agreement,\" a self-referentially odd formulation.","reasoning_cat2":"The intended reference is plainly Section 2.13, and the surrounding subsections are consistent; the mis-citation is one of several in the document.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c208","reasoning_cat1":"A long catalogue of waivers bracketed by two overlapping carve-outs (\"Except as otherwise expressly provided in this Agreement\" and \"(except as otherwise provided in this Agreement)\"), which leaves the scope of the waivers to be worked out against the rest of the document.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 12 requires various notices and Section 9.1's final paragraph waives presentment and demand; the carve-outs are doing real work but no squarely contradictory provision appears.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.12},
{"clause_id":"c209","reasoning_cat1":"Straightforward representations and a continuing covenant to stay informed.","reasoning_cat2":"It refers to \"the financial condition of other guarantors, if any,\" although no Guarantor is identified anywhere in the transaction — a harmless template remnant.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c210","reasoning_cat1":"It waives election-of-remedies defences by reference to \"security for a guaranteed obligation\" and Lender's \"rights of subrogation and reimbursement,\" concepts that belong to guarantors, whereas these parties are co-obligors; the provision also ends with a colon rather than a period.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 13 makes New York law govern, yet this waiver is drafted entirely around Section 580d of the California Code of Civil Procedure — an unresolved tension about which law the waiver even operates under.","prob_cat1":0.29,"prob_cat2":0.29},
{"clause_id":"c211","reasoning_cat1":"Sub-clause (B) refers to \"Agent and Lenders\" — neither term is defined in this bilateral agreement — and the waiver is framed around California antideficiency statutes in a document whose parties are a single Lender and two co-Borrowers.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 13's New York choice of law does not sit comfortably with a waiver expressly built on Sections 580a, 580b, 580d and 726 of the California Code of Civil Procedure, and the undefined \"Agent\" has no referent anywhere in the instrument.","prob_cat1":0.36,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c212","reasoning_cat1":"Clear as to beneficiaries, non-marshalling and reinstatement.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 14.1, 14.2 and 16.7's revival provision.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c213","reasoning_cat1":"Substantively clear subordination of contribution and subrogation claims; the subsection letter is garbled.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 2.13(k) and the Section 2.3(b) waterfall.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c214","reasoning_cat1":"Definite: intercompany debt subordinated and held in trust after a Default.","reasoning_cat2":"It applies on a mere \"Default\" while Section 2.13(j) applies unconditionally; the two are cumulative rather than inconsistent.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c215","reasoning_cat1":"The chapeau makes the making of the initial extension of credit \"conclusively deemed\" to be satisfaction or waiver of every condition, and clause (a) requires filings in offices \"in the opinion of Lender, desirable\" — both are open-textured.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 3.3 imposes separate conditions to all extensions of credit, so the conclusive-waiver language is confined to the initial funding; consistent.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.10},
{"clause_id":"c216","reasoning_cat1":"A closed list of six deliverables; \"form and substance satisfactory to Lender\" is the only soft element.","reasoning_cat2":"It requires Control Agreements and Cash Management Agreements at closing, while Sections 2.6(a)/(c) contemplate the cash management structure being built out over 60 days; a mild sequencing tension.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c217","reasoning_cat1":"Definite; a standard secretary's certificate requirement.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the \"Board of Directors\" and \"Authorized Person\" definitions.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c218","reasoning_cat1":"Definite and narrow.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the \"Governing Documents\" definition and Section 7.3(a).","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c219","reasoning_cat1":"The certificate must be \"dated within 36 days of the Closing Date\" — an unusual figure that the immediately following subsection states as 30 days, so one of the two numbers is wrong on the face of the document.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 3.1(f) uses 30 days for the equivalent foreign-jurisdiction certificates, which makes the discrepancy visible within the same Section.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.17},
{"clause_id":"c220","reasoning_cat1":"The scope of jurisdictions is fixed by whether failure to qualify \"would constitute a Material Adverse Change,\" importing that vague standard into a closing checklist.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 5.8(a) and the Material Adverse Change definition.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c221","reasoning_cat1":"Definite by cross-reference to Section 6.8.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 6.8 does prescribe the required coverage and endorsements; accurate.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c222","reasoning_cat1":"Short and conventional.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 5.9's due authorisation representations.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c223","reasoning_cat1":"Definite, with an express Permitted Protest carve-out.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 6.7 and the Permitted Protest definition.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c224","reasoning_cat1":"An open-ended due diligence condition entirely keyed to results \"satisfactory to Lender,\" and it refers to \"the Loewe-Adler collateral review,\" an extrinsic document nowhere defined.","reasoning_cat2":"It overlaps with Sections 3.1(m), (p), (r) and (s), all of which impose their own satisfaction standards; cumulative rather than contradictory.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c225","reasoning_cat1":"\"Satisfactory to Lender in its sole discretion\" is unqualified, but the condition is narrow and mechanical.","reasoning_cat2":"The four named individuals match the \"Permitted Holders\" list but not the five-name \"Executive Officer\" and \"Validity Agreement Party\" lists.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c226","reasoning_cat1":"Definite in substance; the subsection letter is garbled and \"shall have paid or shall pay\" is loose but workable.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Lender Expenses definition and Section 2.5(c)'s charging authority.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c227","reasoning_cat1":"Short and definite as a condition, though it approves documents not reproduced in the instrument.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the \"Borrower's Required Procedures\" definition, which likewise contemplates pre-closing delivery and approval.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c228","reasoning_cat1":"A single objective dollar test as at a fixed date.","reasoning_cat2":"It matches the Section 7.16(a) covenant floor, but the same $600,000,000 figure is what makes the Section 7.16(b) 0.9% leverage cap impossible to satisfy alongside a $50,000,000 facility.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.14},
{"clause_id":"c229","reasoning_cat1":"It requires a \"Landlord's Waiver and Consent,\" a document type not defined anywhere in the Agreement, for one named address.","reasoning_cat2":"The defined analogue is \"Collateral Access Agreement\" (used in Section 6.9), so the instrument uses two different labels for what appears to be the same instrument.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c230","reasoning_cat1":"Satisfaction is measured by counsel being \"satisfied that such documentation provides Fund and Lender with appropriate rights and remedies\" — a soft but bounded standard.","reasoning_cat2":"Overlaps with Section 3.1(m); consistent.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c231","reasoning_cat1":"The proviso — that the condition \"may be satisfied by Fund providing to Lender such reasonable assurances as Lender may require\" — largely dissolves the substantive requirement that all licences actually be held.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 5.3 and Schedule 5.3 represent that the listed licences are all that is required, so the proviso substitutes assurance for compliance in a way the representation does not contemplate.","prob_cat1":0.23,"prob_cat2":0.14},
{"clause_id":"c232","reasoning_cat1":"A closed list of four review items keyed to Lender's satisfaction; mechanical.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 3.1(j) and Section 6.2's ongoing reporting.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c233","reasoning_cat1":"Two specific, dated financial statements; entirely definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 5.11 and 6.3.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c234","reasoning_cat1":"An eight-item document list, two of which are qualified \"if available\" — a qualifier that lets the condition be satisfied by non-delivery — and the whole is subject to \"form and substance acceptable to Lender\".","reasoning_cat2":"The parallel document list in Eligible Notes Receivable clause (r) has nine items and different timing rules, and Sections 3.3(e), 4.2 and 8.17 each restate the $250,000,000 requirement in slightly different terms.","prob_cat1":0.23,"prob_cat2":0.22},
{"clause_id":"c235","reasoning_cat1":"\"All other documents and legal matters… shall be in form and substance satisfactory to Lender\" is an unbounded catch-all placed after twenty specific conditions — the paradigm general-versus-specific problem.","reasoning_cat2":"The Section 3.1 chapeau deems the making of the initial extension of credit to waive all conditions, which limits the practical bite of the catch-all.","prob_cat1":0.34,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c236","reasoning_cat1":"The section is numbered \"4.2\" in a part of the document that runs 3.1 to 3.7, and the single condition reads \"Manager shall have a hired a full time Controller\"; both are mechanical errors on the face of the provision.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 8.2(c) refers to \"a condition subsequent set forth in Section 3.2,\" a number that does not appear in the document as printed, so the cross-reference chain is broken.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c237","reasoning_cat1":"A conventional bring-down qualified by materiality with an earlier-date carve-out.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Section 5 chapeau, which uses the same formulation.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c238","reasoning_cat1":"A single short condition; the sentence ends without punctuation but the meaning is plain.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the \"Default\" and \"Event of Default\" definitions and Section 8.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c239","reasoning_cat1":"Definite in scope, though \"or other order of any nature\" is a catch-all after three specific forms of relief.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the \"Governmental Authority\" definition and Section 8.6.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c240","reasoning_cat1":"Six words with no measuring date — \"no Material Adverse Change shall have occurred\" gives no baseline from which the change is judged, and the defined term is itself vague.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 5.11 supplies a baseline (\"since the date of the latest financial statements submitted to Lender on or before the Closing Date\") that this condition does not adopt, leaving two different tests for the same concept.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.20},
{"clause_id":"c241","reasoning_cat1":"Definite in amount and content, cross-referring to the Section 3.1(t) document list; \"otherwise reasonably acceptable to Lender\" is the soft element.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 4.2 states the same $250,000,000 holding requirement as a covenant and Section 8.17 as a default trigger with a three-Business-Day cure — three overlapping formulations of one requirement.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.17},
{"clause_id":"c242","reasoning_cat1":"\"A current Borrowing Base Certificate\" leaves \"current\" undefined — a certificate dated when?","reasoning_cat2":"Exhibit B-2 supplies no form (it says \"[form to be provided by Lender]\") and Section 6.2 requires the calculation on each Advance date and monthly, so the required content and vintage are fixed outside this condition.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.20},
{"clause_id":"c243","reasoning_cat1":"A fixed three-year term with a clear early-termination right on default; \"subject to any notice and cure rights otherwise provided\" is the only qualification.","reasoning_cat2":"The document contains a second provision printed as \"3.4\" (Intentionally Blank), and the \"Maturity Date\" definition points to \"Section 3.4\" — so the cross-reference is ambiguous.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c244","reasoning_cat1":"The provision is printed as \"3.4 Intentionally Blank\" when it should be 3.5, duplicating the number of the Term section — a mechanical error visible on the face of the text.","reasoning_cat2":"The \"Maturity Date\" definition cross-refers to Section 3.4, which now identifies two different provisions; the table of contents lists 3.5 as the blank one, confirming the misprint.","prob_cat1":0.28,"prob_cat2":0.28},
{"clause_id":"c245","reasoning_cat1":"Long but carefully sequenced: acceleration on termination, survival of duties and liens, and a release mechanic once everything is paid.","reasoning_cat2":"It says liens remain until Obligations are \"paid in full,\" while Section 1.4 defines repayment in full to exclude contingent indemnification and certain Bank Product Obligations — a definitional overlay that softens the literal words.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.14},
{"clause_id":"c246","reasoning_cat1":"Repetitive but definite: 30 days' notice, full cash payment plus cash collateral and the Applicable Prepayment Premium.","reasoning_cat2":"The Applicable Prepayment Premium is zero after the first anniversary, so the premium requirement here becomes formal only; Section 3.7(b) adds \"if applicable\" while this subsection does not.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.16},

{"clause_id":"c260","reasoning_cat1":"Clear obligation to release and transfer against payment; \"in accordance with the terms of this Agreement\" is the only qualifier.","reasoning_cat2":"That qualifier points to Permitted Dispositions clause (e), which permits sales at not less than 80% of unpaid balance with proceeds to a Cash Management Account — a real constraint not restated here.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c261","reasoning_cat1":"Three enumerated triggers and a defined output; workable.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 4.9(a)-(b) and 6.16's recording obligation.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c262","reasoning_cat1":"A conventional chapeau; it makes the representations both \"as of the date hereof\" and \"as of the Closing Date,\" which are the same date under the Closing Date definition — redundant but harmless.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 3.3(a)'s bring-down and Section 8.11's misrepresentation default.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c263","reasoning_cat1":"\"Good and indefeasible title\" to personal property is an unusual formulation, and the representation is absolute save for Permitted Liens.","reasoning_cat2":"The \"Lien\" definition expressly captures easements, covenants, conditions, restrictions and leases affecting Real Property, while Permitted Liens clause (k) rescues only easements, rights of way and zoning restrictions — so the representation is broader than the carve-out supports.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.23},
{"clause_id":"c264","reasoning_cat1":"Nine sub-representations, several of which restate the eligibility criteria, and clause (i) adds a substantive requirement (development \"located or… expected to be built\") that appears nowhere else and is inherently imprecise.","reasoning_cat2":"The \"Eligible Notes Receivable\" definition itself incorporates \"the representations and warranties respecting Eligible Notes Receivable made in the Loan Documents,\" so definition and representation define each other circularly.","prob_cat1":0.27,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c265","reasoning_cat1":"It gives an unqualified representation that \"all aspects of Borrowers' operations, comply with all applicable federal, state and local laws and regulations\" — absolute, with no materiality or knowledge qualifier, unlike the first sentence of the same section.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 6.10 requires compliance only with laws whose breach could reasonably be expected to cause a Material Adverse Change, so the representation and the covenant apply different standards to the same subject.","prob_cat1":0.23,"prob_cat2":0.24}
]}
