{"judgments": [
{"clause_id":"c266","reasoning_cat1":"\"Fit for such purposes\" is a soft standard, but the representation is trivial in a mortgage-fund context.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Equipment definition and Permitted Dispositions clause (a).","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c267","reasoning_cat1":"The proviso permitting storage of loan files \"in a public warehouse, access to which has been assigned\" is a carve-out from an otherwise flat prohibition, and the sentence switches between \"Borrower Collateral\" and \"the Collateral\".","reasoning_cat2":"Section 7.15 restates the same rule as a covenant and Section 6.9 permits schedule amendment; the three are consistent in substance.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.12},
{"clause_id":"c268","reasoning_cat1":"A short, definite representation about record-keeping.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 6.1 and 4.8(a)(i).","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c269","reasoning_cat1":"Pure schedule reference.","reasoning_cat2":"Schedule 5.7(a) lists both Borrowers as California and states \"SUBSIDIARIES - NONE\"; consistent.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c270","reasoning_cat1":"Pure schedule reference with an update mechanic.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 6.9 does permit amendment of Schedule 5.7(b) on 30 days' notice; accurate.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c271","reasoning_cat1":"Pure schedule reference.","reasoning_cat2":"Schedule 5.7(c) supplies the numbers; consistent with Section 7.5's prohibition on changing them.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c272","reasoning_cat1":"A dated, closed representation.","reasoning_cat2":"Schedule 5.7(d) says \"None\" and Section 4.4(b) handles later-acquired claims; consistent.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c273","reasoning_cat1":"The trailing parenthetical \"(as may be necessary by the applicable laws of such state)\" is garbled and adds nothing, but the substantive representation is standard.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 3.1(e)-(f) and Schedule 5.7(a).","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c274","reasoning_cat1":"The exception \"as described on Schedule 5.8 or in an Offering Circular\" is very wide given how broadly \"Offering Circular\" is defined, and the schedule is expressly \"updated from time to time\".","reasoning_cat2":"Section 6.14's final sentence says no notification \"shall have the effect of amending or modifying this Agreement or any of the Schedules hereto,\" which is hard to square with schedules that update themselves.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.23},
{"clause_id":"c275","reasoning_cat1":"Definite in required content; the self-updating schedule is the only soft feature.","reasoning_cat2":"Schedule 5.7(a) states there are no Subsidiaries, and the \"Subsidiary\" definition excludes most later-formed entities, so this representation has little to operate on; Section 6.14 again resists schedule updating.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.17},
{"clause_id":"c276","reasoning_cat1":"Definite in substance, subject to the same broad \"or in an Offering Circular\" exception.","reasoning_cat2":"Same tension with Section 6.14's no-amendment sentence and with the near-empty Subsidiary group.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.15},
{"clause_id":"c277","reasoning_cat1":"A short, standard corporate-authority representation.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 3.1(c)'s resolutions certificate.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c278","reasoning_cat1":"Four enumerated non-conflict representations with defined carve-outs; conventional.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Permitted Liens and Section 5.9(c).","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c279","reasoning_cat1":"Definite, with an express financing-statement carve-out.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 3.1(q)'s licence condition and Section 4.4(a).","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c280","reasoning_cat1":"A conventional enforceability representation with the usual bankruptcy and equity exceptions.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 8.16's default for contesting validity.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c281","reasoning_cat1":"An absolute present-tense representation that the Liens are \"validly created, perfected, and first priority,\" given at signing before recordings are complete.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 3.1(a) and Section 4.4 contemplate that perfection steps are still being taken, Eligible Notes Receivable clause (s) treats first-priority perfection as something still to be achieved, and Section 8.14 makes any later failure a default — so the representation is in tension with the machinery around it.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.22},
{"clause_id":"c282","reasoning_cat1":"The sentence stacks three carve-outs and a double negative (\"other than matters… that, if decided adversely… reasonably could not be expected to result in a Material Adverse Change\"), so what is actually represented is difficult to extract.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 6.3(g) requires notice of new proceedings using the affirmative formulation, which highlights the awkwardness here but does not contradict it.","prob_cat1":0.29,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c283","reasoning_cat1":"Two clear representations: GAAP conformity and no Material Adverse Change since a stated date.","reasoning_cat2":"It fixes the MAC baseline at the latest pre-closing financial statements, while Section 3.3(d) states the condition with no baseline at all — two different tests for the same defined term.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c284","reasoning_cat1":"Four words plus a defined term; the grammar (\"Each of Borrower and its Subsidiaries\") is loose but the meaning is clear.","reasoning_cat2":"\"Solvent\" is defined by a bare balance-sheet test that omits the usual prongs, so the representation is narrower than its heading (\"Fraudulent Transfer\") suggests.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.10},
{"clause_id":"c285","reasoning_cat1":"A conventional intent representation; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 16.7's revival provision.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c286","reasoning_cat1":"A flat negative representation tied to defined terms.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Benefit Plan and ERISA Affiliate definitions; nothing else in the document imposes ERISA covenants.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c287","reasoning_cat1":"Clauses (a) and (b) are knowledge-qualified while (c) and (d) are absolute — a deliberate but noticeable asymmetry within one representation.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 6.13's covenants and the Environmental Lien definition.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c288","reasoning_cat1":"An absolute two-part representation; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Nothing elsewhere addresses brokers; no conflict.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c289","reasoning_cat1":"\"Necessary to the conduct of its business\" is a soft boundary and \"all material patents… as to which Borrowers… is the owner or is an exclusive licensee\" leaves \"material\" undefined.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 4.4(c) imposes an elaborate IP registration regime that is oddly extensive for these Borrowers, and Schedule 5.16 is self-updating against Section 6.14.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c290","reasoning_cat1":"\"Peaceful and undisturbed possession\" and \"leases material to their business\" are both loose, but the representation is narrow in effect.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 6.6 and 6.11 and Permitted Liens clause (d).","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c291","reasoning_cat1":"A definite schedule-listing representation.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 2.6 and 4.7; the self-updating schedule again sits against Section 6.14's no-amendment sentence.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c292","reasoning_cat1":"The repeated \"(taken as a whole)\" qualifier and the double materiality standard make the reach of the representation less than obvious, but the formula is a market standard.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 6.14 supplies the update duty and expressly denies curative effect; consistent.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c293","reasoning_cat1":"It embeds \"as is satisfactory to Lender\" inside a representation of fact, which conflates a condition with a warranty.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 7.1(b) permits Indebtedness \"set forth on Schedule 5.20,\" so the schedule's accuracy has covenant consequences; consistent.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c294","reasoning_cat1":"It represents about companies that \"will issue\" policies — a forward-looking statement dressed as a present representation.","reasoning_cat2":"The Approved Title Insurance Company definition lets Lender add and remove companies, and the Affiliate definition's 10% deeming rule applies for other purposes, so the no-Affiliate representation has an uncertain measure.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.10},
{"clause_id":"c295","reasoning_cat1":"The duration formula — \"so long as any credit hereunder shall be available and until payment in full of the Obligations\" — is conjunctive and could be read either as requiring both conditions or as running until the later of them.","reasoning_cat2":"The Section 7 chapeau uses a different formula (\"until termination of this Agreement and payment in full\"), so the affirmative and negative covenants have different stated survival periods.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.21},

{"clause_id":"c313","reasoning_cat1":"Four enumerated obligations with specific notice periods; \"reportable quantity\" is an external but ascertainable standard.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 5.14 and 11.3(c) and the Remedial Action definition.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c314","reasoning_cat1":"Clear on its face: prompt notice of prior misstatements, with no curative effect.","reasoning_cat2":"Its closing sentence — that no notification amends \"this Agreement or any of the Schedules hereto\" — is difficult to reconcile with Sections 5.8, 5.16, 5.18 and 5.21, which describe their schedules as \"updated from time to time,\" and with Sections 2.6(c) and 6.9, which expressly authorise schedule amendments.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.29},
{"clause_id":"c315","reasoning_cat1":"Two words in brackets; nothing to construe on its face.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 8.2(a) nonetheless lists Section 6.15 among the covenants whose breach is an immediate Event of Default, so the default provision refers to a covenant that does not exist.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c316","reasoning_cat1":"The opening qualifier \"To the extent necessary to comply with Section 4.2\" (printed with a stray double comma) makes the scope of a delivery covenant depend on another section's threshold, and the closing words require the assignment to be \"recorded by Administrative Borrower on behalf of Lender\".","reasoning_cat2":"Section 4.2 requires delivery only of enough notes to keep $250,000,000 with Lender, while the Eligible Notes Receivable definition (clause (r)) and Section 3.1(t) impose document-delivery requirements note by note — three overlapping and differently scoped delivery regimes.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.23},
{"clause_id":"c317","reasoning_cat1":"An absolute deposit covenant reaching \"all amounts delivered to any Borrower to be held in escrow,\" with an illustrative list introduced by \"including, without limitation\".","reasoning_cat2":"Section 2.6(e) expressly excepts \"accounts belonging to an Account Debtor of Borrower\" from the escrow-deposit requirement, and Section 6.12(d) bars maintaining depository accounts at all — the three provisions cannot all be obeyed as written.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.34},
{"clause_id":"c318","reasoning_cat1":"The covenant's core content is defined by cross-reference to \"Section 3.3(z)\" — a subsection that does not exist, since Section 3.3 runs only to (f) — so the documents the Settlement Agent must collect are not identified; the sentence also ends in a hyphen.","reasoning_cat2":"The intended reference is presumably Section 3.1(t) or the Eligible Notes Receivable document list, but those two lists differ from each other, so the gap cannot be filled unambiguously from the rest of the instrument.","prob_cat1":0.37,"prob_cat2":0.35},
{"clause_id":"c319","reasoning_cat1":"A standard chapeau; the compound duration formula is the only soft feature.","reasoning_cat2":"It differs from the Section 6 chapeau, which omits \"until termination of this Agreement\" — the affirmative and negative covenants therefore state different survival periods.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.19},
{"clause_id":"c320","reasoning_cat1":"A closed exceptions list, but clause (f) permits refinancings only of \"Indebtedness permitted under clause (b)\" while the final exception is lettered \"(z)\" rather than (g), leaving the list's sequence broken.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 7.2's parallel lien covenant refers to replacement Liens \"under Section 7.1(f)\", so the mislettering does not break that chain; \"Indebtedness\" is defined very broadly, which puts pressure on this closed list.","prob_cat1":0.23,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c321","reasoning_cat1":"An absolute negative pledge with a single defined exception; the drafting is compact and clear.","reasoning_cat2":"The \"Lien\" definition sweeps in easements, covenants, conditions and restrictions affecting Real Property, and Permitted Liens clause (c) is garbled (\"so long as such Liens for Approved Debt or subordinated\"), so the covenant's exception is defective at precisely the point that matters for the Permitted Reorganization.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c322","reasoning_cat1":"Definite: no merger or amendment of Governing Documents except pursuant to a Permitted Reorganization.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 7.10 permits distributions \"to the extent required or permitted by Fund's Governing Documents,\" and the Permitted Reorganization definition is itself fixed by an extrinsic written description; the covenant's only escape hatch is therefore undefined in the instrument.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.17},
{"clause_id":"c323","reasoning_cat1":"Repetitive but clear, with two identical carve-outs for a Permitted Reorganization.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 6.12 and 7.3(a).","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c324","reasoning_cat1":"\"All or any substantial part of its assets\" is a vague quantum, and the phrase \"in one transaction or a series of transactions\" leaves the aggregation period unstated.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 7.4 immediately afterwards prohibits disposing of \"any\" assets other than Permitted Dispositions, which makes this subsection wholly redundant — the pair cannot both be given independent effect.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.26},
{"clause_id":"c325","reasoning_cat1":"Read literally it bars disposing of any asset at all outside the Permitted Dispositions list, which would forbid ordinary-course lending, collection and payment activity by a mortgage fund.","reasoning_cat2":"It duplicates and overrides Section 7.3(c)'s \"substantial part\" test, and sits against Section 4.1's flat statement that Borrowers have no authority to dispose of Collateral except for Permitted Dispositions — three provisions covering the same ground with different quantums.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.29}
]}

{"judgments": [
{"clause_id":"c326","reasoning_cat1":"The prohibition covers names, federal employer identification numbers, organizational identification numbers, state of organization and \"organizational identity,\" but the proviso permitting change on 30 days' notice is expressed only as to \"names\" — so four of the five prohibited changes appear to have no escape route.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 5.7 and Schedules 5.7(a)-(c) record the very identifiers this covenant freezes, and Section 4.4(a) covers the financing-statement mechanics; nothing else supplies the missing permission.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c327","reasoning_cat1":"The opening carve-outs — including \"the curtailment in the origination of new loans\" — permit precisely the kind of change the covenant otherwise forbids, and \"the principal nature of its or their business\" is imprecise.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 7.14(b)(i) contemplates proceeds being used to make new loans while this covenant expressly blesses curtailing origination; read with the Permitted Reorganization carve-out, the covenant's remaining field of operation is unclear.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.19},
{"clause_id":"c328","reasoning_cat1":"Three enumerated prohibitions with defined carve-outs; the drafting is dense but each limb is specified.","reasoning_cat2":"Clause (c) restricts amendments only to Indebtedness \"permitted under Section 7.1(b)\" (Schedule 5.20 debt), leaving Subordinated Debt and Approved Debt documents unrestricted here although Section 7.7(b) deals with payments on them.","prob_cat1":0.15,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c329","reasoning_cat1":"One sentence keyed entirely to a defined term; nothing ambiguous in the covenant itself.","reasoning_cat2":"The \"Change of Control\" definition requires Permitted Holders (four named individuals) to own 100% of Manager and Servicer, which is difficult to reconcile with the \"Permitted Reorganization\" definition's contemplation of admitting new members and managers.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.18},
{"clause_id":"c330","reasoning_cat1":"\"Advance notice\" is given no period, and \"in any material respect\" is the only threshold, so both the trigger and the procedure are indeterminate.","reasoning_cat2":"The \"Borrower's Required Procedures\" definition already requires that any amendment have Lender's prior written approval \"given or withheld in Lender's sole discretion,\" a stricter and differently worded control than this covenant's notice-and-consent formulation.","prob_cat1":0.25,"prob_cat2":0.29},
{"clause_id":"c331","reasoning_cat1":"The cross-reference to the quarterly financials is garbled, and clause (a)(ii) permits return-of-capital distributions \"to the extent required or permitted by Fund's Governing Documents\" — a permission whose content lies outside the instrument and could swallow the prohibition.","reasoning_cat2":"\"Restricted Payments\" clause (e) catches any payment to a Stock holder \"not expressly authorized in this Agreement,\" so the breadth of this exception determines the covenant's whole content; Section 7.3(a) restricts amendment of the Governing Documents but does not fix them in the instrument.","prob_cat1":0.29,"prob_cat2":0.27},
{"clause_id":"c332","reasoning_cat1":"Two clear prohibitions with a GAAP carve-out and a specified condition for accounting-firm arrangements.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 6.1, 6.3 and the GAAP definition.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c333","reasoning_cat1":"Short and keyed to defined terms; \"incur any liabilities (including contingent obligations) for or in connection with any Investment\" is broad but bounded.","reasoning_cat2":"Permitted Investments expressly includes making Notes Receivable and holding Real Estate Owned, so the Borrowers' core business is carved out; consistent.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c334","reasoning_cat1":"The section is headed \"Transactions with Affiliates\" but its first sentence prohibits forming or acquiring any Subsidiary, an unrelated subject, and clause (c) then permits \"any other transaction\" satisfying four cumulative conditions.","reasoning_cat2":"The \"Subsidiary\" definition excludes any entity formed after the Closing Date that is not funded with Borrower assets, plus any New Fund and Bar-K, so the no-new-Subsidiary sentence can be circumvented without breach; the Affiliate definition's 10% deeming rule applies specifically \"for purposes of… Section 7.13\".","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.27},
{"clause_id":"c335","reasoning_cat1":"Two enumerated permitted uses; \"working capital and general corporate needs\" is broad but standard.","reasoning_cat2":"Clause (b)(i) permits proceeds only for loans \"evidenced by an Eligible Note Receivable,\" which is a stricter standard than the Note Receivable definition; consistent with Section 6.18's disbursement mechanics.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.11},

{"clause_id":"c350","reasoning_cat1":"\"Material misstatement or misrepresentation\" in any \"warranty, representation, statement, or Record\" is broad but the standard is familiar.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 1.4 deems any transmitted Record a representation of accuracy and completeness, which widens this default considerably; Section 6.14 says notification of a prior misstatement does not cure it.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.14},
{"clause_id":"c351","reasoning_cat1":"A narrow, specific trigger; the grammar (\"the obligations… is terminated\") is loose.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Validity Agreement and Validity Agreement Party definitions and Section 3.1(b)(iii).","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c352","reasoning_cat1":"\"Become unable to perform\" is undefined, and the replacement must have qualifications \"acceptable to Lender\" with no reasonableness standard.","reasoning_cat2":"\"Executive Officer\" names five individuals employed by Manager or Servicer, and Servicer is expressly excluded from the Subsidiary group, so this default reaches persons outside the credit group.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.17},
{"clause_id":"c353","reasoning_cat1":"Definite in structure, with carve-outs for permitted dispositions and for priority permitted by the Loan Documents.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 5.9(e) already represents the Liens are perfected and first priority, and Eligible Notes Receivable clause (s) treats perfection as an ongoing condition — three provisions imposing overlapping perfection standards.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.17},
{"clause_id":"c354","reasoning_cat1":"A short, materiality-qualified trigger.","reasoning_cat2":"It depends entirely on the Servicing Agreement, a document defined but not reproduced; Sections 4.8 and 9.1(e)/(o) also key off it.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.12},
{"clause_id":"c355","reasoning_cat1":"Materiality is fixed by whatever \"Lender in its Permitted Discretion deems to be material,\" and the provision trails off with a dangling \"or.\"","reasoning_cat2":"Section 16.4 makes each provision severable for enforceability purposes, which sits oddly with a default triggered by any material provision being declared void.","prob_cat1":0.29,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c356","reasoning_cat1":"Definite in amount with a stated three-Business-Day cure; \"otherwise reasonably acceptable to Lender\" is the soft element.","reasoning_cat2":"Sections 3.1(t), 3.3(e) and 4.2 each state the same $250,000,000 requirement in different words, so the trigger's precise content depends on which formulation governs.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.18},
{"clause_id":"c357","reasoning_cat1":"A conventional remedies chapeau expressly subject to the Code's commercial-reasonableness requirement, plus a plain acceleration right.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 3.4, 3.6 and 9.2.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c358","reasoning_cat1":"One sentence; entirely clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 3.3(b) and 3.4.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c359","reasoning_cat1":"Clear and carefully limited to future obligations of Lender.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 3.6's survival provisions.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c360","reasoning_cat1":"\"For amounts and upon terms which Lender considers advisable\" gives an unqualified discretion, but the netting mechanic is specified.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 4.5(f) grants the same power under a \"Permitted Discretion\" standard, so the two provisions state different standards for the same act.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.15},
{"clause_id":"c361","reasoning_cat1":"The closing parenthetical charges all amounts incurred as \"Lender Group Expenses,\" a term that is defined nowhere in the Agreement — the cost-shifting mechanism therefore has no defined content.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 1.1 defines \"Lender Expenses,\" which the Section 2.3(b) waterfall pays first and Section 2.5(c) charges to the Loan Account; whether \"Lender Group Expenses\" means the same thing is left to inference.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.33},
{"clause_id":"c362","reasoning_cat1":"Broad self-help powers with a licence to occupy premises; \"considers necessary or reasonable\" is soft but the acts are enumerated.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 10's self-help and Section 4.4(d)'s storage-access assignment; the reference to \"any Guarantor\" is another remnant of an absent party.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c363","reasoning_cat1":"A detailed setoff right with an express waiver of advance notice and a post-hoc notice obligation; carefully drawn.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 2.6(d) (Cash Management Accounts as cash collateral) and Section 9.1(h).","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c364","reasoning_cat1":"One sentence; clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 2.6(d), 3.6 and 9.1(g).","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c365","reasoning_cat1":"The remedies enumerated — ship, finish, repair, complete production of, advertise for sale — belong to an inventory-based facility and have little application to a portfolio of promissory notes, so their reach here is unclear.","reasoning_cat2":"The \"Borrower Collateral\" here consists overwhelmingly of Notes Receivable and Deposit Accounts, and Sections 9.1(e) and (o) supply the remedies actually fitted to that collateral.","prob_cat1":0.21,"prob_cat2":0.17},
{"clause_id":"c366","reasoning_cat1":"Clear and tied to the commercial-reasonableness standard.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Section 9.1 chapeau and Section 9.1(k)'s notice mechanics.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c367","reasoning_cat1":"Definite as to form and 15-day period, though the carve-out for collateral that is \"perishable\" or \"customarily sold on a recognized market\" is inapt for this collateral.","reasoning_cat2":"It directs notice \"as provided in Section 12,\" and Section 12 has a special deemed-sent rule for Code enforcement notices; the two mesh.","prob_cat1":0.15,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c368","reasoning_cat1":"The substance is a single sentence, but the subsection is lettered \"(h)\" in a run that has already used (h) — the enumeration is corrupted at this point.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 8.2 and other provisions cross-refer to lettered subsections elsewhere, so corrupted lettering within Section 9.1 is a live risk of mis-citation.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c369","reasoning_cat1":"Clear, with an express \"to the maximum extent permitted by law\" limit on the ex parte element.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 9.2's cumulative-remedies provision.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c370","reasoning_cat1":"A catch-all reserving \"all other rights and remedies available at law or in equity,\" and the subsection is lettered \"(m)\" duplicating the preceding one.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 9.2 states the same principle again with the qualifier \"not inconsistent herewith,\" which this subsection omits.","prob_cat1":0.21,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c371","reasoning_cat1":"It again charges amounts as \"Lender Group Expenses,\" an undefined term, and folds an automatic-acceleration paragraph into a lettered remedy sub-clause where it does not belong.","reasoning_cat2":"It largely duplicates Section 9.1(e), and the automatic acceleration on Sections 8.4/8.5 sits against the Section 9.1 chapeau's premise that remedies are exercised \"at [Lender's] election\".","prob_cat1":0.29,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c372","reasoning_cat1":"A conventional cumulative-remedies and non-waiver clause.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 9.1(n) and 15.2.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c373","reasoning_cat1":"Lender may act \"in its sole discretion and without prior notice,\" and the closing sentence makes an official payment notice \"conclusive evidence\" of validity — strong but plainly worded.","reasoning_cat2":"Clause (b) lets Lender set reserves against the Borrowing Base or the Maximum Revolver Amount \"as Lender deems necessary,\" with none of the Permitted Discretion or Triggering Event limits that Section 2.1(b) imposes on the same power.","prob_cat1":0.21,"prob_cat2":0.36},
{"clause_id":"c374","reasoning_cat1":"A list of waived formalities; conventional and definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 2.13(e) and 9.1's final paragraph.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c375","reasoning_cat1":"Carefully conditioned on Lender's compliance with the Code, with four enumerated exclusions; a well-built limitation of liability.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 6.8 (insurance) and 11.3, and with the UCC reasonable-care duty preserved in the Section 9.1 chapeau.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c376","reasoning_cat1":"Very broad, with an all-caps clause extending the indemnity to an Indemnified Person's own negligence and \"of any other Person,\" then a carve-out only for gross negligence or wilful misconduct — the interaction of those two sentences is the classic point of contest.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 14.1(b) preserves an assigning Lender's rights under this Section, and Section 16.11 has its own separate indemnity with a narrower carve-out; the two indemnities are not aligned.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c377","reasoning_cat1":"Deemed receipt is set at \"the earlier of the date of actual receipt or three (3) Business Days after the deposit thereof in the mail,\" which as written makes mailing effective only if it precedes actual receipt — the ordinary formula uses \"the earlier of actual receipt or three days,\" so the sentence works only awkwardly; the Lender's Dallas ZIP code is also given as 75244 here and 75254 in the exhibits.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 1.4 says any writing requirement is satisfied by transmission of a Record, which is a looser standard than this Section's prescribed methods.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.19},
{"clause_id":"c378","reasoning_cat1":"An unqualified New York choice of law with a carve-out for contrary provisions in other Loan Documents; clear on its face.","reasoning_cat2":"Sections 2.13(g) and 2.13(h) are drafted entirely around Sections 580a, 580b, 580d and 726 of the California Code of Civil Procedure, and the \"Code\" definition contemplates other states' UCCs governing perfection — so the instrument is not uniformly New York.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.29},
{"clause_id":"c379","reasoning_cat1":"Venue is \"only\" in New York County for the parties, but Lender alone may sue anywhere collateral is found — a conspicuously one-sided allocation of a genuinely reciprocal-looking clause.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 16.3 forbids construing ambiguity against either party, which is the provision that would otherwise answer a contra proferentem challenge to this asymmetry.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.15},
{"clause_id":"c380","reasoning_cat1":"A conventional, mutual jury waiver with an express knowing-and-voluntary recital.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 13(a) and 13(b).","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c381","reasoning_cat1":"\"All, or any ratable part of all\" is odd phrasing, and the final sentence dispenses with the Eligible Transferee requirement for portfolio sales — a wide exception to the stated restriction.","reasoning_cat2":"The \"Eligible Transferee\" definition gives Administrative Borrower an approval right absent an Event of Default, which the portfolio-sale exception overrides; consistent but one-directional.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.12},
{"clause_id":"c382","reasoning_cat1":"It states that an assignment \"shall effect a novation between Borrowers and the Assignee\" — a strong legal consequence stated in passing and without elaboration.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 14.2 says \"No consent to assignment by Lender shall release any Borrower from its Obligations,\" which pulls against the novation language here.","prob_cat1":0.21,"prob_cat2":0.19},
{"clause_id":"c383","reasoning_cat1":"It deems the Agreement amended automatically on receipt of an assignment and acceptance, without Borrower signature; short but consequential.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 15.1 requires that every amendment \"be in writing and signed by Lender and Administrative Borrower,\" so this automatic amendment mechanism contradicts the amendment provision.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c384","reasoning_cat1":"Long and heavily itemised with five enumerated protective conditions; the final proviso is mislettered but each limb is specific.","reasoning_cat2":"Participants are made Indemnified Persons under Section 11.3 while this subsection denies them any direct rights — a deliberate asymmetry rather than a conflict.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.12}
]}

{"judgments": [
{"clause_id":"c385","reasoning_cat1":"A short permission to disclose \"all documents and information,\" expressly made subject to Section 16.8; the subsection letter duplicates an earlier one.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 16.8(f) contains the matching confidentiality exception requiring prospective assignees to agree in writing; consistent.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.10},
{"clause_id":"c386","reasoning_cat1":"It cites \"Regulation A of the Federal Reserve Bank,\" which is a regulation of the Federal Reserve Board, and clause (ii) extends the pledge right to any Person providing financing to Lender or its Affiliates — a much wider category than the Federal Reserve limb suggests.","reasoning_cat2":"It opens \"Any other provision in this Agreement notwithstanding,\" so it overrides the Eligible Transferee limits in Section 14.1(a); that override is deliberate but unqualified.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.12},
{"clause_id":"c387","reasoning_cat1":"\"Absolutely void ab initio\" is garbled in the text, and the sentence \"No consent to assignment by Lender shall release any Borrower from its Obligations\" is awkward — it is not clear whether it addresses Lender's assignments or Borrower's.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 14.1(b) says an assignment by Lender \"shall effect a novation between Borrowers and the Assignee,\" which is difficult to reconcile with this Section's statement that no Borrower is released.","prob_cat1":0.21,"prob_cat2":0.28},
{"clause_id":"c388","reasoning_cat1":"A clear writing-and-signature requirement with a specific-instance limitation on waivers.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 14.1(c) deems the Agreement amended automatically on receipt of an assignment and acceptance without any Borrower signature, which contradicts the requirement here that amendments be signed by Administrative Borrower.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.29},
{"clause_id":"c389","reasoning_cat1":"A conventional non-waiver clause; each sentence is plain.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 9.2 and 15.1.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c390","reasoning_cat1":"One sentence; effectiveness on execution.","reasoning_cat2":"It makes the Agreement effective on execution while Section 3.1 makes the initial credit extension subject to numerous conditions; the two operate at different levels and do not conflict.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c391","reasoning_cat1":"The second sentence — \"Unless the contrary is compelled by the context, everything contained in each Section applies equally to this entire Agreement\" — is an unusual interpretive rule that appears to make every Section's content operate document-wide, which is hard to reconcile with the fact that many Sections are expressly local.","reasoning_cat2":"Read literally against Section 1.4 and the many section-specific provisos (for example the Affiliate definition's proviso limited to Eligible Notes Receivable and Section 7.13), this sentence would extend limitations well beyond their intended reach.","prob_cat1":0.30,"prob_cat2":0.21},
{"clause_id":"c392","reasoning_cat1":"It disclaims any rule of construction against either party and directs interpretation \"according to the ordinary meaning of the words used so as to accomplish fairly the purposes and intentions of all parties\" — two instructions that can pull apart where the ordinary meaning does not serve the purpose.","reasoning_cat2":"It is the provision that would be invoked against contra proferentem in relation to the many one-sided Lender-discretion provisions (Sections 2.1(b), 8.16, 10, 13(b)), which is exactly where it becomes contested.","prob_cat1":0.21,"prob_cat2":0.20},
{"clause_id":"c393","reasoning_cat1":"It declares provisions severable \"for the purpose of determining the legal enforceability of any specific provision\" but never says what follows if a provision is unenforceable — the operative consequence is missing.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 8.16 makes it a default if a provision Lender deems material is declared void, so the instrument treats the same event in two different ways without linking them.","prob_cat1":0.23,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c394","reasoning_cat1":"It directs Borrowers to \"comply with the penultimate sentence of this Section 16.5\" — identifying an obligation only by its position in a paragraph that has plainly been edited, so which sentence governs is not certain.","reasoning_cat2":"The definition of \"Taxes\" is placed here rather than in Section 1.1, and Section 1.1 cross-refers to it accurately; no conflict found.","prob_cat1":0.29,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c395","reasoning_cat1":"A conventional counterparts and electronic-execution clause with an express saving for failure to deliver originals.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 1.4's provision that a writing requirement is satisfied by transmission of a Record.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c396","reasoning_cat1":"Detailed and self-contained; \"or elects to do so upon the reasonable advice of its counsel\" is the only soft element.","reasoning_cat2":"It refers repeatedly to \"any Guarantor,\" a party that does not exist in this transaction, and Section 2.13(i) contains a parallel reinstatement provision for the Borrowers.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c397","reasoning_cat1":"Seven enumerated exceptions, one of which (\"as may be required by statute, decision, or judicial or administrative order, rule, or regulation\") is broad, but the structure is closed and specific.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 14.1(e) and Section 6.3's accountant-contact provisions both operate consistently with it, and Section 14.1(b) preserves the obligation after assignment.","prob_cat1":0.15,"prob_cat2":0.10},
{"clause_id":"c398","reasoning_cat1":"A pure statutory notice with no operative content.","reasoning_cat2":"Nothing else in the instrument turns on it.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c399","reasoning_cat1":"The clause bars contradiction by any other agreement \"before the date hereof,\" which on its face leaves contemporaneous and later agreements untouched, and \"reflects the entire understanding\" is weaker than the usual \"constitutes the entire agreement\".","reasoning_cat2":"The \"Loan Documents\" definition includes \"any other agreement entered into, now or in the future,\" so the integration clause expressly incorporates an open-ended and growing set of documents.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.21},
{"clause_id":"c400","reasoning_cat1":"The appointment is called \"irrevocable\" and then made revocable by written notice in the same sentence, and the indemnity excludes only liability resulting \"solely\" from gross negligence or wilful misconduct — a narrow carve-out that is a familiar point of contest.","reasoning_cat2":"The Section's premise that the Loan Account and Collateral are handled \"in a combined fashion\" sits against Section 6.12's separateness covenants requiring each Borrower to keep its assets distinct from its Affiliates'.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.20},
{"clause_id":"c401","reasoning_cat1":"The form is riddled with unclosed brackets and blanks (\"given to Lender]\", \"commencing on the first day of ,20\"), so the operative election language cannot be read as written.","reasoning_cat2":"The bracketed instruction (\"the first day of a month not less than 3 Business Days after the date of this Notice\") does not match Section 2.12(c), which requires notice before the LIBOR Deadline, and the Dallas ZIP code differs from the one in Section 12.","prob_cat1":0.29,"prob_cat2":0.26},
{"clause_id":"c402","reasoning_cat1":"Paragraph 6 certifies compliance with \"Sections 7.16, and 7.37\" — Section 7.37 does not exist — and paragraphs 2 and 5 make the same representation-bring-down twice with different exceptions.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 6.3(a)(ii) and (c)(iii) require this certificate to demonstrate compliance with Sections 7.16 and 7.17, so the exhibit's cross-reference is wrong; Schedule 3 to the exhibit also repeats the impossible 0.9% Senior Leverage Ratio test.","prob_cat1":0.36,"prob_cat2":0.34},
{"clause_id":"c403","reasoning_cat1":"Like its companion form, this exhibit contains unclosed brackets and blank dates, and the opening quotation mark for \"LIBOR Rate Effective Date\" is missing, so the notice cannot be completed from the text as printed.","reasoning_cat2":"Its \"not less than 3 Business Days\" instruction tracks Section 2.12(b), but Section 2.12(c)'s deemed-election rule makes an affirmative LIBOR Notice largely unnecessary — the form and the mechanism are out of step.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.23},
{"clause_id":"c404","reasoning_cat1":"The account holder is given as \"B-4 PARTNER, LLC,\" which is not the name of either Borrower, and the schedule supplies the definition of \"Designated Account Bank\" that Section 1.1 merely points to.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 6.12(d) forbids Borrowers from maintaining depository accounts other than Cash Management Accounts, and Section 2.6(a) requires all cash management at Wells Fargo after 60 days, yet this Designated Account is at Greater Bay Bank and Section 2.8 requires it be maintained.","prob_cat1":0.21,"prob_cat2":0.22},
{"clause_id":"c405","reasoning_cat1":"A short designation with a redacted account number; the substitution mechanism is clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 2.3(a), 2.6(b) and 2.7.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c406","reasoning_cat1":"Item 2 lists a future, contingent category (\"Once a Permitted Reorganization is implemented, the Subordinated Liens securing Approved Debt\") rather than an existing lien, so what is scheduled is indeterminate.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 2.1(b)(ii) refers to \"any existing Permitted Lien set forth on Schedule P-1 which is specifically identified thereon as entitled to have priority over the Lender's Liens,\" but the schedule makes no such identification for either item.","prob_cat1":0.21,"prob_cat2":0.29},
{"clause_id":"c407","reasoning_cat1":"Two specific licences listed with numbers and dates; nothing ambiguous on its face.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 5.3 represents that this schedule lists all licences required for \"any Borrower\" to conduct its business, yet the schedule lists nothing at all for B-4 Partners LLC, the Manager and Administrative Borrower.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.23},
{"clause_id":"c408","reasoning_cat1":"Two short items identifying where Collateral is kept; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 5.5 and Section 6.9 both refer to it and Section 7.15's public-warehouse proviso contemplates a location the schedule does not list.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.12},
{"clause_id":"c409","reasoning_cat1":"Two lines plus a flat statement that there are no Subsidiaries.","reasoning_cat2":"The \"SUBSIDIARIES - NONE\" entry makes the whole \"and its Subsidiaries\" apparatus of Sections 5 through 7 inoperative at closing, and the Subsidiary definition's carve-outs make it likely to stay that way.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c410","reasoning_cat1":"A single address; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Matches the address in Sections 3.1(o) and 12 and Schedule 5.5.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c411","reasoning_cat1":"The identification numbers are rendered as \"Jo021\" and \"EEE0060,\" which cannot be actual organisational identification numbers as printed.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 5.7(c) represents that these numbers are accurate and Section 7.5 forbids changing them, so an unreadable schedule undermines both.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c412","reasoning_cat1":"One word; nothing to construe.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 5.7(d) and Section 4.4(b).","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c413","reasoning_cat1":"A long narrative that describes redemption rights as existing only \"in the discretion of the Manager\" while also reporting 50 pending redemption requests, and states that \"all or substantially all\" capital contributions have been made — a hedged factual assertion in a document meant to be a complete and accurate description.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 5.8(b) requires this schedule to be \"complete and accurate\" and excepts anything described \"in an Offering Circular\"; the redemption machinery it describes is what Section 7.10 and the Permitted Reorganization definition are built around, and Section 8.9(x) makes a default on capital obligations to members an Event of Default.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.26},
{"clause_id":"c414","reasoning_cat1":"A narrative disclosure of two specific matters; the second sentence is loosely written but identifies the matter.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 5.10 carves out \"actions to enforce Account Debtor obligations or Account Debtor bankruptcies,\" which appears to cover both disclosed matters anyway.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c415","reasoning_cat1":"One word; nothing to construe.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 5.16 nonetheless represents that Borrowers own or license all IP \"necessary to the conduct of its business,\" and Section 4.4(c) imposes an elaborate patent, trademark and copyright registration regime — an apparatus with no subject matter.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.21},
{"clause_id":"c416","reasoning_cat1":"A short list of accounts with partially redacted numbers; definite in structure.","reasoning_cat2":"Every listed account is at Greater Bay Bank, which cannot be squared with Section 2.6(a)'s requirement that Wells Fargo be the only Cash Management Bank 60 days after closing, nor with Section 6.12(d)'s prohibition on maintaining other depository accounts.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.27},
{"clause_id":"c417","reasoning_cat1":"Two short items with a cross-reference to Schedule 5.8; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 7.1(b) permits only \"Indebtedness set forth on Schedule 5.20,\" so the single Fremont Bank loan is the entire permitted legacy debt; Schedule P-1 lists the same lien consistently.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c418","reasoning_cat1":"The two-column list has collapsed so that company names run into one another (\"Commonwealth Land Title Insurance _ Company\", \"Land America Title Insurance Company -Ticor Title Insurance Company Co.\"), leaving it genuinely uncertain which entities are approved.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 5.21 represents this is \"a true and complete list\" and the \"Approved Title Insurance Company\" definition, the \"Settlement Agent\" definition and Eligible Notes Receivable clause (h) all depend on it.","prob_cat1":0.28,"prob_cat2":0.17}
